proposal.title: Vakoskzim: a memory-safe image decoder
proposal.summary: Vakoskzim builds a memory-safe image decoder for developers of messaging and mail clients.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Image decoders written in unsafe languages are a frequent source of exploits. Developers of messaging and mail clients depend on memory-safe parsing every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a memory-safe image decoder called Vakoskzim. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Memory-safe parsing is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/vakoskzim/vakoskzim, which 61 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on memory-safe parsing for 12 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/vakoskzim/vakoskzim. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 53950.00 EUR for 96 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 650.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Image decoders written in unsafe languages are a frequent source of exploits. Developers of messaging and mail clients depend on memory-safe parsing every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a memory-safe image decoder called Vakoskzim. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Memory-safe parsing is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/vakoskzim/vakoskzim, which 61 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on memory-safe parsing for 12 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/vakoskzim/vakoskzim. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.
